pairs.question: What happens to my health when I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: When you quit smoking, you'll begin to see almost immediate improvements to your health. It's a great step towards a healthier life!
pairs.evidence: When you quit smoking, you'll begin to see almost immediate improvements to your health.

pairs.question: Is it ever too late to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: It's never too late to quit smoking! You can start your journey towards a smoke-free life at any time.
pairs.evidence: It's never too late to quit and it's easier to stop smoking with the right support.

pairs.question: What should I do if I slip up while trying to quit?
pairs.answer: If you slip up, you can learn how to handle cravings and manage withdrawal symptoms. It's important to get back on track!
pairs.evidence: Learn how to handle cravings, manage withdrawal symptoms, and get back on track if you slip up.

pairs.question: What will my quit plan help me with?
pairs.answer: Your quit plan will show how much money you can save and give tips for managing smoking triggers. It's a great tool to stay smoke-free!
pairs.evidence: It will help you prepare for your quit date, show how much money you can save, and give tips for managing smoking triggers.

pairs.question: What benefits can I expect from quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Quitting smoking can make life better for you and those around you. You'll enjoy a healthier, smoke-free life!
pairs.evidence: Learn how quitting smoking can make life better for you and those around you.

pairs.question: What about my sense of taste and smell?
pairs.answer: Your lungs are clearing out mucus and your senses of taste and smell are improving. This is a positive change you can expect after quitting.
pairs.evidence: Your lungs are clearing out mucus and your senses of taste and smell are improving.

pairs.question: How does quitting affect my energy levels?
pairs.answer: Your energy will be increasing after you quit smoking. This is part of the positive changes your body goes through.
pairs.evidence: Also your energy will be increasing.

pairs.question: What happens to my carbon monoxide levels when I quit?
pairs.answer: Your carbon monoxide levels have dropped to that of a non-smoker. This is a significant improvement for your health.
pairs.evidence: Your carbon monoxide levels have dropped to that of a non-smoker.

pairs.question: Will quitting smoking reduce my risk of lung cancer?
pairs.answer: More great news! Your risk of death from lung cancer will have halved compared with a smoker's. This is a major benefit of quitting.
pairs.evidence: More great news! Your risk of death from lung cancer will have halved compared with a smoker's.

pairs.question: Can I really quit smoking for good?
pairs.answer: With clear steps and support, your plan will give you the tools to quit smoking and stay smoke-free for good. It's a big change, but you can do it!
pairs.evidence: With clear steps and support, your plan will give you the tools to quit smoking and stay smoke-free for good.

pairs.question: What happens to my risk of death from lung cancer if I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Your risk of death from lung cancer will have halved compared with a smoker's. That's a significant improvement for your health!
pairs.evidence: Your risk of death from lung cancer will have halved compared with a smoker's.

pairs.question: How can I stay motivated while trying to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Using the NHS Quit Smoking app can really help you stay motivated. It allows you to record your goals and see your progress.
pairs.evidence: The NHS Quit Smoking app really helped me. I liked seeing my progress. Recording my goals and reading other people’s stories kept me motivated.

pairs.question: Is it too late for me to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: It's never too late to quit. Quitting is one of the best choices you can make for yourself!
pairs.evidence: It's never too late to quit. Imagine a healthier body, a calmer mind and more money in your pocket. Quitting is one of the best choices you can make for yourself.

pairs.question: What can I do to help with cravings when I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: You can use lozenges to help with cravings. Some people also find that using a vape around smokers can help them quit for good.
pairs.evidence: I used lozenges to help with cravings. However, when I’m around smokers I use a vape. This helped me quit for good.

pairs.question: How long do I need to be smoke-free to increase my chances of quitting for good?
pairs.answer: Once you reach 28 days smoke-free, you're much more likely to quit for good! That's a great milestone to aim for.
pairs.evidence: Once you reach 28 days smoke-free, you're much more likely to quit for good!

pairs.question: What kind of support can I get to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: You can get help from your local Stop Smoking Service. They can provide you with the support you need to quit successfully.
pairs.evidence: But what worked was choosing a quit date and getting help from my local Stop Smoking Service.

pairs.question: What are some benefits of quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Quitting smoking can lead to a healthier body, a calmer mind, and more money in your pocket. It's a positive change!
pairs.evidence: Imagine a healthier body, a calmer mind and more money in your pocket.

pairs.question: How can I track my financial savings after quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: The NHS Quit Smoking app shows the massive financial savings made after quitting. It's a great way to see how much you're saving!
pairs.evidence: The NHS Quit Smoking app also helped. It shows the massive financial savings made.
